(Nasdaq: TRDA) today announced positive topline data from Cohort 1 of the double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple ascending dose (MAD) portion of the Phase 1/2 ELEVATE-45-201 clinical study of ENTR-601-45 in ambulatory participants with a confirmed mutation in the DMD gene amenable to exon 45 skipping.
Topline results met the primary objectives of favorable safety and tolerability.

“Importantly, establishing a favorable safety profile at this initial dose in a three dose MAD study is the essential foundation for escalating to higher doses, and seeing any dystrophin produced in participants this young, with such low baseline levels, is an encouraging early signal.” Highlights from the topline results of Cohort 1 of ELEVATE-45-201 include: Dystrophin measured by western blot and normalized to MHC; Dystrophin values are actual observed values, including values <LLOQ; Two participants in the ENTR-601-45 group had baseline dystrophin levels <LLOQ and >LOD; LLOQ for dystrophin was 0.25%; LOD for dystrophin was 0.1%; Biopsy performed at baseline; LLOQ : Lower limit of quantification; LOD : Limit of detection; MHC : Myosin heavy chain.
